locator: Heading "## Intended outcome" (insert a section before it)
current: ## Intended outcome
proposed:
## Problem

A customer contacts the Bank several times about the same issue. Calls, chats, cases, complaints and status changes sit in separate records. The employee has to reconstruct the history by hand and may miss the actual blocker, repeat an earlier request or transfer the customer again.

## Intended outcome
note: The page had no problem statement. Text is the "Problem" paragraph of the source proposal, with "the Bank" capitalized.

locator: First paragraph under "## Intended outcome"
current: Help the servicing employee understand what happened, verify the current state of a customer issue and identify the next permitted step. The proposed workspace brings together relevant contacts, case history, authoritative status and approved service guidance with links to the underlying evidence.
proposed: The customer receives one accurate explanation and a clear next step, with fewer repeat contacts and a faster confirmed resolution. To that end the service employee is helped to understand what happened, verify the current state of the issue and identify the next permitted step. The proposed workspace brings together relevant contacts, case history, authoritative status and approved service guidance, with links to the underlying evidence.
note: The source proposal's outcome is the customer's (fewer repeat contacts, faster confirmed resolution); the summary had kept only the means. Also "servicing employee" becomes "service employee", as on the landing page.

locator: Second paragraph under "## Intended outcome"
current: The employee reviews the interpretation, owns the response and approves any operational action. AI-generated interpretations remain distinguishable from verified facts.
proposed:
The employee reviews the interpretation, owns the response and approves any operational action. AI-generated interpretations remain distinguishable from verified facts.

Customer intelligence here means the reusable result of that work: a source-linked record of the customer's service history, the action taken and its outcome, kept for the stated purpose and available to later service journeys.

## What would be built

For each eligible case the employee sees the customer's current request, a short timeline of earlier contacts and actions, the verified current status, the likely reason the issue is still open, the approved procedure with the proposed next step, and links to the underlying records. The likely reason is marked as an inference.

Banking systems remain the source of facts. A context service assembles the minimum authorized view for the journey, an assistant with limited authority interprets it within a fixed workflow, and the employee decides. AI does not establish customer identity, payment status, eligibility, deadlines or permissions.
note: The title promises "customer intelligence" and the page never explained it; the page also never said what would be built. Both paragraphs condense the source proposal ("What is built", "Target pilot architecture", "Where GenAI adds value").

## Decisions still to be taken

Three decisions are separate. Approval of the proposal would authorize mobilization, baseline work, definition of controls and preparation of the pilot. Controlled live use needs its own readiness decision. Approval of the pilot does not authorize a wider rollout.

This page is a summary. The full proposal contains the business case, three candidate journey charters, a technical pilot blueprint, journey technical profiles and a platform capability and readiness map.
note: Restores the sponsor, the benefit owner and the independence of measurement; adds what approval would and would not authorize (source: "Candidate Project Charters", last paragraph of the introduction); tells the reader that a full proposal exists. Where the full proposal can be read is question 8.

locator: First paragraph under "## Approach"
current: The environment supports exploration while keeping each experiment accountable: a named owner, permitted data, limited access, a time and cost budget, reproducible evaluation and an explicit decision at the end.
proposed:
The environment supports exploration while keeping each experiment under control. Every experiment has a named owner, permitted data, limited access, a time and cost budget, a reproducible evaluation and an explicit decision at the end.

Data enters the environment only as read-only extracts, with a named owner for each source. Nothing is written back to a source system, and personal data is masked, redacted or excluded before it enters.

The shared environment may support successive experiments. Each experiment has its own scope, time limit, evidence and outcome.
note: Adds the data rule, which is the firmest content of the original concept (read-only ETL, no production write-back, PII assessment) and was reduced to "permitted data". Moves the paragraph on successive experiments here from "Guidance to develop". Experiments are not "accountable"; people are.
